questions.q: What are the four fundamentals of life used to assess where you are?
a: Health, work, play and love
Money, status, family and travel
Health, wealth, faith and friendship
Work, rest, learning and service
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists health, work, play and love as the areas to balance.

questions.q: What is the Good Time Journal for?
a: Recording activities and how they make you feel, to find flow
Scheduling meetings so you never waste an hour
Tracking how much money you spend on leisure
Listing famous people whose careers you admire
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the journal captures what energizes you and where you lose track of time.

questions.q: What does flow feel like, according to the summary?
a: Being so absorbed in an activity that time disappears
Feeling calm because nothing important is happening
Working quickly to clear a long list of tasks
Resting after a period of intense effort
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes flow as being entranced by what you are doing.

questions.q: Why does the book recommend keeping several possible paths open?
a: Many different routes can lead to a fulfilling life
Only one path can ever produce real happiness
Having options lets you avoid committing to anything
A single plan always works out exactly as written
questions.why: Lesson 3 says there is no single true path and options are worth exploring.

questions.q: What happened to the young man who took three internships one after another?
a: He enjoyed advising friends so much that he became a career counselor
He was hired full-time by the first company he tried
He decided that all three fields were wrong for him
He abandoned his career plans to travel instead
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses his story to show how exploring several paths can reveal an unexpected direction.
